- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +5% above peak to prevent overshoot.  
- If sentiment is rising (last 3 values > 0.6) and forecast is falling, adjust downward by 2–3% to reflect bullish momentum.  
- If forecast mean is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 30d, apply a 5% downward bias correction for next forecast.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing 3-day moving average of forecast.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days below 70 after peak), forecast should trend back toward 70–72, not continue downward.  
- For early horizon (1–7 days), forecast should align with sentiment direction; for late horizon (15–30d), allow 3–5% lag to reflect market inertia.
